NOTE: This file is the Phase 2 centralized tolerance-policy source for the six harness modes, and IS the single source for consume's numeric tolerances: test_compare_cpp_python.py's _COMPARE_COLS loads from here at import time. Round 4 correction pass (2026-08-29) expanded consume from 14 to 76 keys so every one of consume_summary.csv's 66 real scientific columns, plus the 10 component-only percent-consumed quantities consume_components.csv exposes that consume_summary.csv does not (see _output_contract.py), has an explicit classification -- most newly added are honestly unverified (no comparison exists), not invented tolerances. Round 4 ALSO corrected a round-3 mistake: RotDW1kCon and SmoDur were wrongly described as newly-discovered, apparently-unrelated divergences; Gate 0's own F-23 Consequences paragraph (gate0/04-findings.md) already named all four case-6 fields (DufCon, RotDW1kCon, SmoDur, TotCon) together as consequences of the SAME Northeast duff-routing defect -- corrected, no new finding ID created. Every non-consume mode's entries now also carry an explicit covers_columns (and column_group where the same output column is legitimately classified by more than one equation-route entry) so coverage is machine-checked, not asserted. See tests/unit/test_tolerance_policy_completeness.py for the schema/coverage tests and tests/cpp_parity_live/_output_contract.py for the metadata/scientific column contract and the component-field resolution rule.

all.justification: calc_bark_thickness() always raises KeyError('FOFEM_BrkThck_Vsp') — the bundled species_codes_lut.csv lacks that column entirely (F-19). No Python-vs-C++ numeric comparison is possible until this is fixed. The C++ oracle path itself (this Phase 2 golden) is unaffected and fully functional; SMT_CalcBarkThick's own unit conversion (inches vs Python's cm) is unit-consistent per the crosswalk once the Python side is restored.

Three independent divergences identified in the Gate 0 crosswalk: (a) C++ zeroes a tree's contribution when f_Hgt<=0 OR f_Dia<=0; Python excludes only dbh<=0/NaN and still credits crown area to a zero/negative-height tree; (b) Python's species-to-equation mapping depends on a caller-supplied tree_code_dict — with the default None, every tree is assigned equation 39 ('Other'), which does not match C++'s per-species FVS index lookup; (c) Python assumes one tree per acre per record while C++ callers supply an explicit per-acre count. None of these are numeric-tolerance-bridgeable; each requires a Python-side fix or an explicit input-contract change before any atol/rtol is meaningful.

herb.justification: Calc_Herb routing precedence is inverted for the Pine Flatwoods cover group specifically (F-11): C++ tests Pine Flatwoods first, then region SouthEast; Python's np.select lists them in the opposite order. shrub.justification: consm_shrub has three independent defects: routing precedence inverted for three cover groups (F-13/F-14), Eq 236 off by 1-2 orders of magnitude from a missing exp() plus a unit round-trip bug (F-15), and silent NaN instead of an error for out-of-domain inputs (F-16). No atol/rtol can honestly bound this until the Python side is fixed.
